data.comment: Permissions tab: small capitals header of the role names above the matrix.

data.name: Security_ColHowCaps
data.comment: Permissions tab: small capitals header of the column that says how each role gets its privileges (directly, inherited, owner …).

data.name: Security_ColumnGrants
data.comment: Permissions tab: small capitals heading above the privileges granted on single columns.

data.name: Security_KindOptionTable
data.comment: Permissions tab: choice in the picker of what kind of object to show.

data.name: Security_KindOptionSequence
data.comment: Permissions tab: choice in the picker of what kind of object to show.

data.name: Security_KindOptionSchema
data.comment: Permissions tab: choice in the picker of what kind of object to show.

data.name: Security_KindOptionDatabase
data.comment: Permissions tab: choice in the picker of what kind of object to show.

data.name: Security_KindOptionFunction
data.comment: Permissions tab: choice in the picker of what kind of object to show.

data.name: Security_KindOptionType
data.comment: Permissions tab: choice in the picker of what kind of object to show.

data.name: Security_NoPendingChanges
data.comment: Permissions tab: label beside Edit grants while nothing is staged.

data.name: Security_PendingChanges_one
data.comment: Permissions tab: label beside Edit grants. Plural. {count} is how many changes are staged, such as 3.

data.name: Security_PendingChanges_other
data.comment: Permissions tab: label beside Edit grants. Plural. {count} is how many changes are staged, such as 3.

data.name: Security_DefaultAclNote
data.value: Aucun GRANT ni REVOKE n'a jamais été exécuté sur cet objet. {owner} le possède et détient tous les droits ; tous les autres n'ont que ce que Postgres accorde par défaut pour ce type d'objet.
data.comment: Permissions tab: banner shown when the object's privileges were never changed. GRANT and REVOKE are SQL. {owner} is the owning role's name, such as postgres.

data.name: Security_CellTip
data.comment: Permissions tab: tooltip of a cell of the matrix. {privilege} is the SQL privilege such as SELECT; {explanation} says why the role has it or not, such as inherited from readers.

data.name: Security_CellTipPendingRevoke
data.comment: Permissions tab: second line of a cell's tooltip when a REVOKE is staged for it. REVOKE is SQL.

data.name: Security_CellTipPendingGrant
data.comment: Permissions tab: second line of a cell's tooltip when a GRANT is staged for it. GRANT is SQL.

data.name: Security_CellTipNotRevocable
data.value: Le fait d'être propriétaire ou superuser n'est pas un droit accordé : il ne peut donc pas être révoqué.
data.comment: Permissions tab: second line of a cell's tooltip when the privilege comes from owning the object or being a superuser.

data.name: Security_SourceSuperuser
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the role has everything because it is a superuser.

data.name: Security_SourceOwner
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the role has everything because it owns the object.

data.name: Security_SourceVia
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the role has the privileges through its membership in another role. {role} is that group role, such as readers.

data.name: Security_SourceDirect
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the privilege was granted to the role itself.

data.name: Security_SourcePublic
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the privilege was granted to PUBLIC, the SQL keyword for every role. A translation may keep it.

data.name: Security_SourceUnknown
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the server says the role has the privilege but the catalog does not show why.

data.name: Security_PublicGrantee
data.comment: The grantee shown for a privilege or policy that applies to every role: the SQL keyword PUBLIC. A translation may keep it. A role that is merely named PUBLIC is shown in quotation marks by the app, so the two can be told apart.

data.name: Security_ExplainNone
data.comment: Why a role does or does not have a privilege (tooltip of a matrix cell, and part of the sentence under the matrix): it was not granted.

data.name: Security_ExplainDirectBy
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it was granted to the role itself. {grantor} is the role that ran the GRANT, such as postgres.

data.name: Security_ExplainDirect
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it was granted to the role itself, by a role we cannot name.

data.name: Security_ExplainInherited
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: through its membership in a group role. {role} is that group, such as readers.

data.name: Security_ExplainPublic
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it was granted to PUBLIC, the SQL keyword for every role.

data.name: Security_ExplainOwner
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it owns the object.

data.name: Security_ExplainSuperuser
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it is a superuser.

data.name: Security_ExplainUnknown
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: the server says yes but the catalog the app can read does not explain it.

data.name: Security_ListSeparator
data.comment: Separator between the items of a list of privileges, such as SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE. Put a space after it if your language uses one.

data.name: Security_ListAnd
data.comment: Joins a list of privileges with and: {head} is the items before the last one, joined by the list separator (SELECT, INSERT), {last} is the last one (UPDATE).

data.name: Security_ListOr
data.comment: Joins a list of privileges with or: {head} is the items before the last one, joined by the list separator (SELECT, INSERT), {last} is the last one (UPDATE).

data.name: Security_SentenceNone
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. {role} is a role name, {object} the object such as sales.orders.

data.name: Security_SentenceNoneBlocked
data.value: {role} n'a aucun droit sur {object}. {role} n'a de plus pas USAGE sur le schéma {schema}, ce qui bloque l'accès à tout son contenu.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. {role} is a role name, {object} the object such as sales.orders, {schema} its schema. USAGE is a SQL privilege name.

data.name: Security_SentenceBlocked_one
data.value: {role} détient {privileges} sur {object} — {explanation} — mais ne peut pas l'utiliser : il lui manque USAGE sur le schéma {schema}, dont tout objet a d'abord besoin.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Plural: several privileges are held but unusable. {role} is a role name, {privileges} a list such as SELECT and INSERT, {object} the object, {explanation} why the role has them, {schema} the schema. "them" is the privileges. USAGE is a SQL privilege name.

data.name: Security_SentenceBlocked_other
data.value: {role} détient {privileges} sur {object} — {explanation} — mais ne peut pas les utiliser : il lui manque USAGE sur le schéma {schema}, dont tout objet a d'abord besoin.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Plural: several privileges are held but unusable. {role} is a role name, {privileges} a list such as SELECT and INSERT, {object} the object, {explanation} why the role has them, {schema} the schema. "them" is the privileges. USAGE is a SQL privilege name.

data.name: Security_SentenceBlockedDenied_one
data.value: {role} détient {privileges} sur {object} — {explanation} — mais ne peut pas l'utiliser : il lui manque USAGE sur le schéma {schema}, dont tout objet a d'abord besoin. Il n'a pas non plus le droit {denied}.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Plural: several privileges are held but unusable, and others are missing. Same placeholders as Security_SentenceBlocked_other, plus {denied}, the missing privileges as a list joined with or, such as INSERT or UPDATE.

data.name: Security_SentenceBlockedDenied_other
data.value: {role} détient {privileges} sur {object} — {explanation} — mais ne peut pas les utiliser : il lui manque USAGE sur le schéma {schema}, dont tout objet a d'abord besoin. Il n'a pas non plus le droit {denied}.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Plural: several privileges are held but unusable, and others are missing. Same placeholders as Security_SentenceBlocked_other, plus {denied}, the missing privileges as a list joined with or, such as INSERT or UPDATE.

data.name: Security_SentenceCan
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. {role} is a role name, {privileges} what it can do as SQL verbs such as SELECT and INSERT, {object} the object such as sales.orders, {explanation} why, such as inherited from readers.

data.name: Security_SentenceCanCannot
data.value: {role} peut effectuer {privileges} sur {object} — {explanation}. Il ne peut pas effectuer {denied}.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Same placeholders as Security_SentenceCan, plus {denied}, what the role cannot do as a list joined with or, such as INSERT or UPDATE.

data.name: Security_CopyAsSql
data.comment: Default privileges tab: button that opens the selected row's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES statement in a new query tab.

data.name: Security_CopyAsSqlTip
data.value: Ouvrir dans un nouvel onglet l'instruction ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES que représente cette ligne
data.comment: Default privileges tab: tooltip of the Copy as SQL button. ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES is SQL.

data.name: Security_ColCreatedBy
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the role that will create the objects the default applies to.

data.name: Security_ColInSchema
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the schema the default applies in.

data.name: Security_ColAppliesTo
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the kind of object the default applies to (tables, sequences …).

data.name: Security_ColGrantee
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the role that gets the privileges.

data.name: Security_ColPrivileges
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the list of privileges.

data.name: Security_AllSchemas
data.comment: Shown instead of a schema name in the Default privileges tab (the default applies in every schema) and as the first choice of the schema filter in the Row-level security tab. Keep the parentheses.

data.name: Security_AppliesToTables
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to tables.

data.name: Security_AppliesToSequences
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to sequences.

data.name: Security_AppliesToFunctions
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to functions.

data.name: Security_AppliesToTypes
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to data types.

data.name: Security_AppliesToSchemas
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to schemas.

data.name: Security_NoDefaultPrivileges
data.value: Aucun droit par défaut n'est configuré.
data.comment: Default privileges tab: heading shown when there are none.

data.name: Security_NoDefaultPrivilegesHint
data.value: Tout objet créé à partir de maintenant n'aura que les valeurs par défaut intégrées : son propriétaire a tout, PUBLIC a EXECUTE sur les fonctions et USAGE sur les types, et rien du tout sur les tables et séquences.
data.comment: Default privileges tab: explanation under the heading shown when there are none. PUBLIC, EXECUTE and USAGE are SQL words and stay as written.

data.name: Security_DefaultsNoteExisting
data.value: Ils n'affectent pas les objets déjà existants. Ils s'appliquent aux objets créés à partir de maintenant, ce qui explique pourquoi un GRANT … ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA … et un droit par défaut sont tous deux nécessaires : aucun ne remplace l'autre.
data.comment: Default privileges tab: first note under the list. The GRANT statement is SQL and stays as written.

data.name: Security_DefaultsNoteCreator
data.value: Ils sont liés au rôle qui crée l'objet, pas au schéma où il atterrit. Un droit par défaut défini pour le mauvais créateur s'exécute sans erreur et ne fait silencieusement rien — la raison la plus courante pour laquelle on dit avoir défini des droits par défaut sans que rien ne change.
data.comment: Default privileges tab: second note under the list.

data.name: Security_DefaultPrivilegesTabTitle
data.comment: Title of the query tab that opens with an ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES statement. {owner} is the role that creates the objects, such as app_rw.

data.name: Security_SchemaFilterTip
data.value: Seuls les schémas qui utilisent la sécurité par ligne quelque part sont listés
data.comment: Row-level security tab: tooltip of the schema filter.

data.name: Security_CopyPolicyAsSql
data.comment: Row-level security tab: button that opens the selected policy's CREATE POLICY statement in a new query tab.

data.name: Security_CopyPolicyAsSqlTip
data.value: Ouvrir dans un nouvel onglet l'instruction CREATE POLICY de la politique sélectionnée — Postgres ne peut pas modifier sur place la commande ni le caractère permissif d'une politique : on la modifie donc en la recréant
data.comment: Row-level security tab: tooltip of the Copy policy as SQL button. CREATE POLICY is SQL.

data.name: Security_PoliciesInert
data.comment: Row-level security tab, list of tables: warning on a table that has policies but row-level security is switched off. RLS means row-level security.

data.name: Security_PoliciesDoNothing
data.comment: Row-level security tab: heading of a warning about a table whose policies have no effect.

data.name: Security_PoliciesDoNothingHint
data.value: La sécurité par ligne n'a jamais été activée pour cette table : toutes les politiques ci-dessous sont donc inactives et chaque rôle lit chaque ligne. Écrire des politiques ne l'active pas — ALTER TABLE … ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, si.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: explanation of the warning. The ALTER TABLE statement is SQL and stays as written.

data.name: Security_YouBypass
data.comment: Row-level security tab: heading of a warning that the connected role is not subject to the policies.

data.name: Security_DeniesEverything
data.value: La sécurité par ligne est activée et cette table n'a aucune politique : elle ne renvoie donc aucune ligne à tout rôle qui ne la contourne pas. C'est l'état de refus par défaut, pas une erreur de configuration en soi.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: note on a table with row-level security on and no policies.

data.name: Security_PolicyAppliesTo
data.comment: Row-level security tab: label before the roles a policy applies to.

data.name: Security_PolicyUsing
data.value: USING — quelles lignes existantes sont visibles
data.comment: Row-level security tab: label above a policy's USING expression. USING is the SQL keyword and stays first.

data.name: Security_PolicyWithCheck
data.value: WITH CHECK — quelles lignes nouvelles ou modifiées sont autorisées
data.comment: Row-level security tab: label above a policy's WITH CHECK expression. WITH CHECK is the SQL keyword and stays first.

data.name: Security_NoPolicies
data.comment: Row-level security tab: shown in the details of a table without policies.

data.name: Security_NoRlsTables
data.value: Aucune table avec sécurité par ligne.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: heading shown when no table has row-level security or a policy.

data.name: Security_NoRlsTablesHint
data.value: Les tables apparaissent ici dès que la sécurité par ligne est activée ou qu'elles portent une politique, dans n'importe quel ordre.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: explanation under the heading shown when no table has row-level security.

data.name: Security_RlsEnabledForce
data.comment: Row-level security tab: state of a table. Row-level security is on and also applies to the table's owner (SQL option FORCE).

data.name: Security_RlsEnabled
data.comment: Row-level security tab: state of a table. Row-level security is on.

data.name: Security_RlsNotEnabled
data.comment: Row-level security tab: state of a table. Row-level security is off.

data.name: Security_PolicyCount_one
data.comment: Row-level security tab: how many policies a table has. Plural. {count} is the number, such as 3.

data.name: Security_PolicyCount_other
data.comment: Row-level security tab: how many policies a table has. Plural. {count} is the number, such as 3.

data.name: Security_PolicyForEveryone
data.comment: Row-level security tab: the policy applies to every role (the SQL keyword PUBLIC).

data.name: Security_BypassUnknown
data.value: {role} voit toutes les lignes de cette table, quoi que disent les politiques ci-dessous. Ses attributs de rôle n'ont pas pu être lus : c'est donc soit un rôle superuser ou BYPASSRLS (qui contourne toutes les tables, toujours), soit le propriétaire d'une table qui n'est pas en FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: warning body. {role} is the connected role. BYPASSRLS and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY are SQL and stay as written.

data.name: Security_BypassSuperuser
data.value: {role} est un superuser : il contourne donc la sécurité par ligne sur toutes les tables du cluster. C'est inconditionnel : FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY ne lui applique pas les politiques. Testez ces politiques avec le rôle que votre application utilise pour se connecter.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: warning body. {role} is the connected role. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is SQL and stays as written.

data.name: Security_BypassAttribute
data.value: {role} a l'attribut BYPASSRLS : il contourne donc la sécurité par ligne sur toutes les tables, toujours. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY ne lui applique pas les politiques. Testez ces politiques avec le rôle que votre application utilise pour se connecter.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: warning body. {role} is the connected role. BYPASSRLS and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY are SQL and stay as written.

data.name: Security_BypassOwner
data.value: {role} possède cette table, ou est membre du rôle qui la possède, et la table n'est pas en FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY — les politiques ci-dessous ne lui sont donc pas appliquées, alors qu'elles le sont à tous les autres rôles. ALTER TABLE … FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY les applique aussi au propriétaire.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: warning body. {role} is the connected role. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and the ALTER TABLE statement are SQL and stay as written.

data.name: Security_ObjectDropped
data.value: {object} n'existe plus — il a été supprimé depuis la construction de la liste des objets.
data.comment: Error line of the Roles and Permissions window. {object} is the name of the object, such as sales.orders.

data.name: Restore_OwnersKept
data.value: Les objets conservent leurs propriétaires et droits d'origine de la sauvegarde.
data.comment: Restore window, form: note under Keep owners and permissions, when it is checked.

data.name: Restore_OwnersNotKept
data.value: Vous serez propriétaire de tout ce qui est restauré, et les droits de la sauvegarde sont ignorés.
data.comment: Restore window, form: note under Keep owners and permissions, when it is unchecked.

data.name: Restore_ProgressCreatingDatabase
data.comment: Restore window, while running: first progress line when a new database is created. {name} is its name.

data.name: Restore_ProgressFinishing
data.comment: Restore window, while running: progress line at the end.

data.name: Restore_ItemRows
data.comment: Restore window, while running: progress line. {name} is a table, such as public.orders.

data.name: Restore_ItemCreating
data.comment: Restore window, while running: progress line. {name} is the kind and name of an object, such as TABLE public.customers; the kind is PostgreSQL's own word and stays as it is.

data.name: Restore_ItemDropping
data.comment: Restore window, while running: progress line. {name} is the kind and name of an object, such as TABLE public.customers; the kind is PostgreSQL's own word and stays as it is.

data.name: Restore_OpenFailed
data.comment: Restore window, after a restore: shown when the new window could not be opened. {database} is a database name; {reason} is the error's own message.

data.name: Restore_ResultRestored
data.comment: Restore window, after a successful restore: heading. {database} is a database name, such as shop_restored; {time} is the duration, such as 0:12.

data.name: Restore_ResultNew
data.value: {database} est une nouvelle base sur ce serveur.
data.comment: Restore window, after a successful restore into a new database: detail. {database} is its name.

data.name: Restore_ResultRefreshed
data.value: L'arborescence des schémas a été actualisée.
data.comment: Restore window, after a successful restore into the current database: detail.

data.name: Restore_ResultStopped
data.comment: Restore window, after the user stopped a restore: heading.

data.name: Restore_ResultFailed
data.comment: Restore window, after a failed restore: heading.

data.name: Restore_FailedNoReason
data.value: pg_restore s'est arrêté sans dire pourquoi.
data.comment: Restore window, after a failure with no error message. pg_restore is a program name.

data.name: Restore_UnchangedRemoved
data.value: Rien n'a été restauré, et la nouvelle base {database} a de nouveau été supprimée.
data.comment: Restore window, after a stop or a failure: detail. {database} is the new database's name.

data.name: Restore_UnchangedMaybeCreated
data.value: Rien n'a été restauré. Si la base {database} a été créée, elle est vide ; supprimez-la quand vous voulez.
data.comment: Restore window, after a stop or a failure when the new database could not be removed. {database} is its name.

data.name: Restore_UnchangedCurrent
data.value: Rien n'a été modifié : la restauration s'exécute en une seule transaction, et {database} est comme avant.
data.comment: Restore window, after a stop or a failure of a restore into the current database. {database} is its name.

data.name: Backup_FolderMissing
data.comment: Backup window, after a failure: the folder chosen for the file is missing. {folder} is a folder path.

data.name: Backup_CheckToolsFolderDump
data.value: Vérifiez dans Paramètres, onglet Données, le dossier que pgNimbus utilise pour pg_dump.
data.comment: Backup window, after a failure: hint when pg_dump could not be started. pgNimbus is the product name; Settings and Data are names of a page and a tab.

data.name: Restore_CheckToolsFolder
data.value: Vérifiez dans Paramètres, onglet Données, le dossier que pgNimbus utilise pour pg_restore.
data.comment: Restore window, after a failure: hint when pg_restore could not be started. pgNimbus is the product name; Settings and Data are names of a page and a tab.

data.name: Backup_SaveFailed
data.value: La sauvegarde est terminée, mais elle n'a pas pu être enregistrée sous {path} : {reason}. Elle se trouve toujours dans {partial}.
data.comment: Backup window, after a failure: the finished file could not be moved to its name. {path} is the chosen file; {reason} is the system's own message; {partial} is a temporary file path.

data.name: Backup_CouldNotStart
data.comment: Backup and Restore windows, after a failure: the program could not be started. {file} is a file name, such as pg_dump.exe; {reason} is the system's own message.

data.name: Restore_ServerThroughSsh
data.comment: Restore window, in the question before restoring into the current database: the server's host when the connection goes through an SSH tunnel. {host} is a host name, such as db.example.com.

data.name: Restore_HintNoCreateDb
data.value: Votre rôle ne peut pas créer de bases de données. Restaurez plutôt dans cette base, ou utilisez un rôle avec CREATEDB.
data.comment: Restore window, after a failure: hint. CREATEDB is a PostgreSQL role attribute and stays as it is.

data.name: Restore_HintPickName
data.comment: Restore window, after a failure: hint when a database of that name exists.

data.name: Restore_CreateFailed
data.comment: Restore window, after a failure: the new database could not be created. {database} is its name; {reason} is the server's own message.

data.name: Backup_LogDropped_one
data.comment: First line of the log shown after a backup or restore, when the oldest lines were dropped. Plural. {count} is the number of lines, such as 120.

data.name: Backup_LogDropped_other
data.comment: First line of the log shown after a backup or restore, when the oldest lines were dropped. Plural. {count} is the number of lines, such as 120.

data.name: Backup_ReasonNoPgDump
data.value: il n'y a pas de pg_dump dans ce dossier
data.comment: Reason a folder holds no usable PostgreSQL program. It is placed inside a sentence such as "Settings point pgNimbus at C:\tools, but there's no pg_dump in this folder." Write it as a clause that fits there; do not end it with a full stop.

data.name: Backup_ReasonNoPgRestore
data.value: pg_dump est présent, mais pas pg_restore
data.comment: Reason a folder holds no usable PostgreSQL program. It is placed inside a sentence; write it as a clause that fits there, without a full stop.

data.name: Backup_ReasonCantStart
data.value: il ne peut pas être démarré ({detail})
data.comment: Reason a PostgreSQL program is not usable. It is placed inside a sentence; write it as a clause without a full stop. {detail} is the system's own message.

data.name: Backup_ReasonTimeout
data.value: il n'a pas répondu en {seconds} secondes
data.comment: Reason a PostgreSQL program is not usable. It is placed inside a sentence; write it as a clause without a full stop. {seconds} is a number, such as 10.

data.name: Backup_ReasonDllMissing
data.value: il ne démarre pas : une bibliothèque dont il a besoin est absente
data.comment: Reason a PostgreSQL program is not usable (Windows could not load a library). It is placed inside a sentence; write it as a clause without a full stop.

data.name: Backup_ReasonWrongCpu
data.value: il ne démarre pas : il est conçu pour un autre processeur
data.comment: Reason a PostgreSQL program is not usable. It is placed inside a sentence; write it as a clause without a full stop.

data.name: Backup_ReasonNoVersion
data.value: il n'a pas indiqué de version de PostgreSQL
data.comment: Reason a PostgreSQL program is not usable. It is placed inside a sentence; write it as a clause without a full stop.

data.name: Backup_ReasonExitedLine
data.value: il s'est terminé avec le code {code} : {line}
data.comment: Reason a PostgreSQL program is not usable or a run failed. It is placed inside a sentence; write it as a clause without a full stop. {code} is an exit code, such as 2; {line} is the program's own first error line.

data.name: Backup_ReasonExited
data.value: il s'est terminé avec le code {code}
data.comment: Reason a PostgreSQL program is not usable or a run failed. It is placed inside a sentence; write it as a clause without a full stop. {code} is an exit code, such as 2.

data.name: Backup_HintPassword
data.value: Le serveur a refusé le mot de passe avec lequel pgNimbus a connecté cette fenêtre. S'il a changé depuis, reconnectez-vous et réessayez.
data.comment: Hint under a backup or restore error. pgNimbus is the product name.

data.name: Backup_HintRoleMissing
data.value: La sauvegarde nomme un rôle que ce serveur n'a pas. Désactivez Conserver propriétaires et droits pour devenir propriétaire de tout, ou créez d'abord le rôle.
data.comment: Hint under a restore error. Keep owners and permissions is the name of a check box in the Restore window.

data.name: Backup_HintPointsOutside
data.value: La sauvegarde fait référence à quelque chose qu'elle ne contient pas, par exemple une table d'un autre schéma. Une sauvegarde de schéma ou de table a besoin de ce vers quoi elle pointe : restaurez-la dans une base qui le contient, comme celle d'où elle vient.
data.comment: Hint under a restore error.

data.name: Backup_HintMustBeOwner
data.value: Un élément de la sauvegarde appartient à un rôle au nom duquel vous ne pouvez pas agir. Désactivez Conserver propriétaires et droits, ou restaurez avec ce rôle.
data.comment: Hint under a restore error. Keep owners and permissions is the name of a check box in the Restore window.

data.name: Backup_HintRestorePermission
data.value: Votre rôle ne peut pas créer ici tout ce que contient la sauvegarde. Restaurez dans une nouvelle base, dont vous êtes propriétaire, ou utilisez un rôle qui le peut.
data.comment: Hint under a restore error.

data.name: Backup_HintToolTooOld
data.value: Ce pg_dump est plus ancien que le serveur. Installez-en un plus récent ; Paramètres, onglet Données, indique lequel pgNimbus utilise.
data.comment: Hint under a backup error. pg_dump is a program name; Settings and Data are names of a page and a tab; pgNimbus is the product name.

data.name: Backup_HintBackupPermission
data.value: Votre rôle ne peut pas lire tout ce que cela couvre. Utilisez un rôle qui le peut, ou sauvegardez un schéma ou une table qu'il peut lire.
data.comment: Hint under a backup error.

data.name: Backup_HintCertificate
data.value: Le certificat du serveur n'a pas pu être vérifié. Vérifiez les paramètres SSL de la connexion et le certificat racine.
data.comment: Hint under a backup or restore error.

data.name: Backup_HintUnreachableTunnel
data.value: {tool} n'a pas pu joindre le serveur via le tunnel SSH de cette fenêtre. Gardez la fenêtre connectée pendant l'exécution.
data.comment: Hint under a backup or restore error when the connection goes through an SSH tunnel. {tool} is pg_dump or pg_restore.

data.name: Backup_HintUnreachable
data.value: {tool} n'a pas pu joindre le serveur. Vérifiez qu'il est en marche et que cet ordinateur peut l'atteindre.
data.comment: Hint under a backup or restore error. {tool} is pg_dump or pg_restore.

data.name: Backup_HintCannotWrite
data.value: Le fichier n'a pas pu être écrit. Vérifiez que le dossier existe, que vous pouvez y écrire et que le disque a de la place.
data.comment: Hint under a backup or restore error.

data.name: Backup_HintObjectGone
data.value: Un élément couvert a été supprimé ou renommé depuis le chargement de la fenêtre. Actualisez le schéma et réessayez.
data.comment: Hint under a backup error.

data.name: Backup_GuideWinDownload
data.value: Téléchargez le programme d'installation de PostgreSQL {version} pour Windows (Windows x86-64) depuis EDB (source officielle).
data.comment: Install steps for Windows, step 1. {version} is a PostgreSQL release, such as 18. EDB is a company name.

data.name: Backup_GuideWinDownloadLink
data.comment: Install steps for Windows, step 1: button that opens EDB's download page.

data.name: Backup_GuideWinRun
data.value: Lancez-le. Sur la page Select Components, ne cochez que Command Line Tools : ni le serveur, ni pgAdmin, ni Stack Builder ne sont nécessaires. Gardez le dossier proposé.
data.comment: Install steps for Windows, step 2. Select Components, Command Line Tools, pgAdmin and Stack Builder are names in the installer; write them as the installer shows them in your language if it is translated, else keep them.

data.name: Backup_GuideWinWinget
data.value: Ou installez la même chose depuis un terminal, et ne choisissez que Command Line Tools quand le programme d'installation le demande :
data.comment: Install steps for Windows, step 3. A command to copy is shown under it.

data.name: Backup_GuideWinLookAgain
data.value: Cliquez ensuite sur Rechercher à nouveau. pgNimbus trouve C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\{version}\bin tout seul.
data.comment: Install steps for Windows, last step. Look Again is the name of a button; {version} is a PostgreSQL release, such as 18; the folder path is kept as it is.

data.name: Backup_GuideMacBrew
data.value: Installez les programmes clients de PostgreSQL avec Homebrew :
data.comment: Install steps for macOS with Homebrew, step 1. A command to copy is shown under it.
